issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power or a stall, sometimes at highway speed, and the car may not restart. Warning messages about the throttle or low fuel pressure can appear first.
issues.why: The fuel pump in the tank can fail and stop delivering fuel. Stellantis recalled 2017-2019 Giulias and 2018-2019 Stelvios to replace the fuel delivery module; at first owners got interim letters while parts were prepared.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and ask the dealer about parts timing. If the car loses power, get safely off the road and have it towed rather than restarting and driving on.

issues.t: Limp mode with 'Service Electronic Throttle' warning
issues.sym: The car suddenly goes into reduced power with messages such as 'Service Electronic Throttle' or 'Throttle Unavailable', a check engine light, and sometimes a stall. Codes for low fuel pressure or low turbo boost are common.
issues.why: On many of these cars the cause is low fuel pressure from a weak fuel pump, which the engine computer protects against by cutting power. Throttle and boost faults can cause the same messages.
issues.next: Have the codes read rather than just cleared. Ask the dealer whether the fuel pump recall applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Misfires can overheat the catalytic converter (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a flashing check engine light, or a burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: If the 2.0L engine misfires, unburned fuel can overheat the catalytic converter and damage nearby wiring and engine parts.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. The recall fix is an engine computer software update plus a check for stored codes.

issues.t: Brake line can rub on a coolant hose clamp (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking, a soft brake pedal, a brake warning light, or a burning smell from fluid hitting the exhaust.
issues.why: On some all-wheel-drive Giulias with the 280 hp engine, a brake line can touch a coolant hose clamp and wear through.
issues.next: If the brake pedal feels soft or you see fluid, don't drive the car. The recall adds a bracket and replaces any damaged line.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise may not switch off after wheel slip (recall)
issues.sym: After the traction control steps in on a slippery road, the adaptive cruise control may not turn off when you try to cancel it.
issues.why: A software fault in the brake system module could keep adaptive cruise active after a wheel-slip event.
issues.next: Use the brake pedal to take control if cruise won't cancel. Have the dealer install the brake module software update.

issues.t: Carbon ceramic brake rotors can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Unusual noise or vibration when braking hard, or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: On cars with the optional carbon ceramic brakes, the brake system could clamp too hard in some maneuvers and crack a rotor.
issues.next: Have the brake module software update done and the rotors inspected.

issues.t: Contaminated brake fluid from the factory (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing at first. Over time, brake performance can drop or brake parts can be damaged.
issues.why: Some 2018 Giulias and Stelvios were filled at the factory with contaminated brake fluid.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects the brake system and replaces parts as needed.

issues.t: Water can leak into the body control module (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers, lights or the horn stop working or act up, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get into the body control module and its connectors on some 2018 Stelvios, corroding them.
issues.next: Have the dealer add the extra sealing from the recall and check the module for corrosion.

issues.t: Liftgate can open by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The power liftgate opens on its own while the vehicle is moving slowly.
issues.why: Water can get into the liftgate wiring and opening switch on some 2018 Stelvios, corroding them and triggering the switch.
issues.next: Don't leave loose items against the liftgate. Have the dealer install the added water protection.

issues.t: Wipers stuck on low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The windshield wipers only run on low speed, even when set higher, making it hard to see in heavy rain.
issues.why: Wiper software on some 2018 Stelvios wrongly thinks the motor is overheating and limits it to low speed.
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the wiper motor under the recall.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads higher than the real level (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge or range shows more fuel than is in the tank, so you can run out unexpectedly.
issues.why: Body control module software could misreport the fuel level.
issues.next: Track fill-ups by mileage until the software update is done at the dealer.

issues.t: Quadrifoglio coolant hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant on the ground, a low coolant warning, a sweet smell, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: An engine coolant hose on some Stelvio Quadrifoglios was made with weak webbing and can leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the temperature climbs, stop and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Fuel line pressure sensor housing can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell, a fuel leak in the engine bay, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The housing of a pressure sensor in the fuel line can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed. The recall replaces the housing as needed.

issues.t: ABS pump can fail under hard braking (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and brake warning lights, a harder brake pedal, or loss of anti-lock function after a hard stop.
issues.why: A shaft inside the ABS hydraulic control unit can separate during hard braking, reducing brake assist and disabling ABS.
issues.next: Have the ABS hydraulic unit replaced under the recall. Leave extra stopping distance until then.

issues.t: Rear brake discs can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding, clunking or vibration from the rear when braking, or reduced braking.
issues.why: The rear brake discs on some cars can fracture during normal use.
issues.next: Have the rear discs and pads replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Tires with too low a load rating (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice, but the tires may be overloaded with a full car.
issues.why: Some cars were fitted with tires rated for less load than required.
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the tires under the recall.

issues.t: Brake pedal can come loose from the booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or goes to the floor, and the car won't slow down normally.
issues.why: The fastener that links the brake pedal to the brake booster may not have been assembled correctly, so the pedal can disconnect.
issues.next: If the pedal feels odd, don't drive the car. The dealer inspects and repairs the connection under the recall.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle sensor may stop a front airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag or seat belt warning light, or no warning at all.
issues.why: The seat belt buckle switch sensor may not be properly connected, so a front airbag may not deploy as intended. It covers 2017-2024 Giulias and 2018-2025 Stelvios.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer repair the connection.

issues.t: Wrong tire information on the door label (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure or size on the door-jamb placard doesn't match what your car needs.
issues.why: The tire placard and related labels were printed with incorrect pressure and size information. Some 2023 Stelvios repaired once needed a second label correction.
issues.next: Use the corrected labels mailed by the automaker, or have a dealer put them on.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen stays blank, freezes or shows a distorted picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A circuit board and software problem in the radio can stop the camera image from showing properly.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look over your shoulder until fixed. The dealer updates the software and replaces the radio if needed.

issues.t: Misfires from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rough idle or shaking, and misfire codes for cylinders 1 to 4.
issues.why: The ignition coils on these engines can fail. A service bulletin tells technicians to replace all four coils when only misfire codes are present.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard, since misfires can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Oil leak from the timing cover
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the front of the engine, drips under the car, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The timing cover bolts on 2.0L engines built through early May 2024 can lose their tightness, letting oil seep out.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed. A service bulletin has the shop re-tighten the cover bolts and reseal the cover if it still leaks.

issues.t: Quadrifoglio limp mode from engine computer software
issues.sym: Check engine light and the car going into limp mode with reduced power.
issues.why: Engine computer software on the twin-turbo V6 can set a processor fault and trigger limp mode.
issues.next: Have a dealer reprogram both engine computers to the latest software.

issues.t: Corroded ground straps can melt wiring
issues.sym: Smoke or a burned plastic smell from under the hood, electrical faults, or warning lights for the ABS and other systems.
issues.why: Owners report corroded engine-to-body ground straps sending current through other wiring, which overheats and melts harnesses.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic or see smoke, stop and shut the car off. Have the ground straps and harnesses inspected.

issues.t: Coolant loss and burning coolant smell
issues.sym: A sweet burning smell, the coolant level dropping, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: Owners report coolant leaks, including radiator failures, and in some cases coolant mixing with oil.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. If it keeps dropping, have the cooling system pressure-tested before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Battery keeps going flat
issues.sym: The car won't start, the battery warning comes on, or the start-stop system acts up. Some owners replace batteries repeatedly.
issues.why: Owners report batteries that don't hold a charge. These cars have a lot of electronics and a start-stop system that put extra load on the battery.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested, and check for anything draining power with the car off.

issues.t: Sunroof glass shatters or won't close
issues.sym: The sunroof glass breaks without anything hitting it, or the sunroof won't close.
issues.why: Several owners report spontaneous sunroof glass breakage or sunroof mechanism failure.
issues.next: Cover the opening to keep rain out and have the sunroof inspected. Ask the dealer about warranty or goodwill help.

issues.t: Headlights fail, aim wrong or get water inside
issues.sym: A headlight goes out, the beam points too high and blinds other drivers, or moisture collects inside the lens.
issues.why: Owners report headlight failures, misaimed beams and water entering the headlight assembly.
issues.next: Have the headlight aim and the assembly checked. A water-filled headlight usually needs a new assembly.

issues.t: Instrument cluster goes black or reboots
issues.sym: The digital gauges or screen go dark or restart while driving, or the fuel gauge jumps.
issues.why: Owners report instrument cluster and infotainment faults; software updates or replacement units are common fixes.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for software updates and record the fault while it's under warranty.

issues.t: Brake system warnings and brakes grabbing
issues.sym: A brake system fault message, brakes that engage on their own or lose pressure, or the parking brake staying on.
issues.why: The Giulia uses an electronic brake-by-wire system, and owners report faults that trigger warnings or unexpected braking.
issues.next: Treat any brake warning seriously and have the car towed if the brakes feel wrong. Ask the dealer to check for brake module software updates.

issues.t: Exterior trim moldings come loose
issues.sym: Wind noise or flapping from a loose roof molding at the back of the roof, or a rear door belt molding that sits partly out of place.
issues.why: Service bulletins cover a roof molding that isn't fully clipped in and rear door belt moldings that partly detach.
issues.next: Have the dealer refit or replace the molding before it comes off at speed.
